svg.title: getBill: how billing data is collected from AWS, Azure and Google Cloud
svg.desc: The architecture shows how getBill copies the daily billing exports of AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud customer accounts into a data lake in AWS, converts them to FOCUS 1.2 and shows them in Amazon Quick dashboards.

text.tspan: getBill: how billing data is collected from AWS, Azure and Google Cloud
Each cloud writes a daily billing export inside the customer's own account. getBill copies the exports into its data lake in AWS, converts them to one format, and shows them in dashboards.
AWS: payer accounts that hold the customers' bills
This account is used when a
getBill account in FPT's AWS organization
This account holds the data lake, the processing jobs and the dashboards.
How the data moves, step by step
Every day, AWS Data Exports writes a CUR 2.0 export and a FOCUS 1.2 export to an S3 bucket in each payer
account. In FPT's payer accounts, AWS Billing Conductor groups the accounts of each customer and sets the price
An Amazon S3 replication rule copies each new export file from the payer account into the raw zone of getBill's
Every day, Azure Cost Management writes a FOCUS export to a storage account in the customer's Azure tenant.
An EventBridge schedule starts a Lambda function. The function signs in with the customer's Entra ID app
registration, whose secret is kept in Secrets Manager, and copies the new files into the raw zone.
An AWS Glue job uses the Google BigQuery connector to read the customer's billing export tables and writes them
to the raw zone. It signs in with a Google service account key that is kept in Secrets Manager. Google Cloud
support is planned for a later release.
Step Functions runs AWS Glue ETL jobs that convert every source to FOCUS 1.2, add FPT's resale price, and write
Parquet files to the curated zone.
The Glue Data Catalog holds the table definitions, and Athena views join and summarize the curated data.
Amazon Quick dashboards query the Athena views. Row-level security in Amazon Quick shows each customer only
SNS and SES send budget and anomaly alerts. DynamoDB lists every customer and cloud account, Parameter Store
holds the settings of each connection, IAM roles give each job only the access it needs, KMS encrypts the stored
data, and CloudTrail records every access.

Sources: AWS Cloud Financial Management blog, "Automating multi-cloud cost management at scale: A2A's FinOps platform powered by AWS"; AWS Data Exports, Amazon S3 replication and AWS Billing Conductor documentation;
Microsoft Cost Management exports documentation; Google Cloud Billing export to BigQuery documentation. Icons are the official AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud icon sets.
